evidence_frontier: Completed confirmations show widths 8,10,12 meet the gate (candidate_correct ≥ control_correct‑10) with fresh seeds; w8 100‑epoch (seeds 42‑46) passed, w10 100‑epoch (201‑205) passed, w12 100‑epoch (101‑105) passed. The next step is to test an untried width.
analysis: Observation: Local widths 8,10,12 each achieved aggregate Q.ANT correct within 10 of the width‑16 control under independent seed sets, indicating that substantial compression does not severely degrade performance. Hypothesis: The performance advantage continues smoothly such that width 13 will also satisfy the gate.
hypothesis: Increasing local width from 8 toward 16 yields non‑monotonic but generally improving Q.ANT correct counts; we hypothesize that width 13 will satisfy the preregistered gate, confirming a smooth performance scaling across widths.

proposal.title: 100‑epoch Confirmation of Local Width 13 on ECG200
proposal.research_question: Does local width 13 for the Alpha5 model satisfy the preregistered performance gate relative to the width‑16 control on ECG200 under fresh seeds?
proposal.rationale: Having established that widths 8,10,12 meet the gate, testing width 13 provides a more complete width‑response curve and assesses whether the trend holds for higher intermediate compression levels.
proposal.success_criteria: alpha13.aggregate_qant_correct >= alpha5_w16_control.aggregate_qant_correct - 10 (candidate_correct ≥ control_correct - 10 on 500 aggregated test predictions).
proposal.risks: If width 13 fails the gate, it may indicate a non‑linear performance drop, questioning the assumption of smooth scaling; also limited test set size may lead to variance in aggregate counts.
